questions.question: How does using structured specifications reduce problems associated with natural‑language specifications?

options.A: By eliminating the need for any documentation altogether.
options.B: By increasing variability in the specification.
options.C: By imposing uniformity and organizing requirements, thus reducing variability.
options.D: By allowing unrestricted use of informal language.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Structured specifications impose uniformity and organize requirements, which reduces variability compared to natural language specifications [Page 23].

---

questions.question: Which statement best describes the role of use cases in software modeling?

options.A: They replace all class diagrams in UML.
options.B: They provide a graphical and textual way to describe user‑system interactions.
options.C: They are only used for low‑level code generation.
options.D: They focus solely on database schema design.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] Use cases describe interactions between users and a system using both a graphical model and structured text, and are a fundamental UML feature [Page 25].

questions.question: What is the purpose of describing side effects of an operation in a specification?

options.A: To list the aesthetic design choices of the UI.
options.B: To identify any changes the operation may cause beyond its primary function.
options.C: To document the hardware requirements of the system.
options.D: To provide a marketing tagline for the feature.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] A side‑effects description captures any additional changes an operation may cause, beyond its main purpose [Page 23].

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] The citation includes author, year, article title, journal, volume, issue, and DOI, but does not provide a URL for the PDF [Page 36].

questions.question: Which of the following best defines unit testing according to the provided material?

options.A: Testing the entire integrated system after deployment.
options.B: Testing individual program components such as methods or classes.
options.C: Testing only the user interface for visual consistency.
options.D: Testing the performance of the network infrastructure.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] Unit testing involves testing program components like methods or object classes individually [Page 41].

---

questions.question: When designing unit tests for a method, why is it recommended to call the routine with different input parameters?

options.A: To ensure the method fails every time.
options.B: To verify that the method behaves correctly across a range of scenarios.
options.C: To reduce the number of test cases needed.
options.D: To avoid using any test‑case design approaches.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Varying input parameters helps confirm correct behavior under diverse conditions, as suggested for function or method tests [Page 41].

questions.question: How do programming‑language constructs such as alternatives and iteration improve structured specifications?

options.A: They make the specification harder to read for non‑programmers.
options.B: They allow the specification to express conditional and repeated behavior directly.
options.C: They eliminate the need for any documentation.
options.D: They convert the specification into executable code automatically.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Using constructs like alternatives and iteration lets specifications explicitly represent conditional and repetitive logic [Page 23].

questions.question: What visual technique is mentioned for highlighting key elements in structured language notations?

options.A: Adding background music to the document.
options.C: Printing the document on colored paper only.
options.D: Embedding video clips within the text.

questions.explanation:
[Bloom: Remember | Difficulty: Easy] Structured language notations may highlight key elements using shading or different fonts [Page 23].

questions.question: Why did use cases become a fundamental feature of UML after being introduced in the Objectory method?

options.A: Because they replaced all other diagram types in UML.
options.B: Because they offered a clear way to model user‑system interactions, fitting UML’s goal of standardization.
options.C: Because they required no textual description, only graphics.
options.D: Because they were the only method supported by early UML tools.

questions.explanation: [Bloom: Understand | Difficulty: Medium] Use cases, first introduced in Objectory, provide a clear model of interactions and were adopted into UML as a core feature [Page 25].
